quotes.text: With the rise of AI right now, a lot of people are concerned about losing jobs. I'm going to work to make sure that AI is just like the technology we're seeing here. It actually empowers Wisconsin workers. It doesn't put them out of business.

The rise of AI is a very scary thing, especially to my generation. We stand to lose many jobs, we don't even know how many. But the United States has always led the way when it comes to technological advancements. I was just talking to someone today whose plan is to put these data centers in space. We need to give these decisions to the local municipalities. States and counties know far better what is better for their neighbors than the federal government. The federal government is only interested in taking your money and sending it elsewhere.

When it comes to data centers, I think the real key, President Trump himself said this, is local control. Let the local towns, communities, counties decide what they want. And, you know, they will be able to deal with the consequences far better than a government that's out in D.C. making decisions.

I've grown up with technology my entire life, and I understand how AI has the ability to destroy life in Northern Wisconsin as we know it. But I also know that if done properly, it has the power to empower workers in a way we've never seen before. I like to think about the nail gun. The nail gun didn't put roofers out of business. It actually made roofers able to build more roofs. And I think with the right leadership in DC, we can actually make sure that AI is benefiting American workers.

Now if you were to ask me do I want a data center in Hayward, Wisconsin where I live? Absolutely not. But I'll tell you what, the federal government does not have a role in stepping in and telling local municipalities what they can and cannot do.

President Trump was actually very clear with this. He said, if you're a local municipality and you don't want one, you don't need one. President Trump truly listens to the people. I mean, when we look at issues like the data center issue, it's very clear. People in northern Wisconsin don't want it. But I can't say the same for Kansas. I've never been there. If they want one, it's not the federal government's job to step in and say no. It's the state or local government.
